newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 2.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Foreign investment interest is now centred on small issues, an encouraging change from the past when interest focused on major increases of share capital. Brokers say the new trend is due to new issues having a greater potential for profit.
--The state's new issue of treasury bills goes up for subscription today with an interest rate of 9.6 percent. The state hopes to raise 250-270 billion drachmas from the issue.
--The buyout of Stella pasta makers by St George Mills last week has already had an effect, with the price war between Misko and Melissa coming to an abrupt halt.

--There's gold in Sappes, Thrace and Australian firm Danae Resources is prospecting for it, according to reports from Melbourne. Danae says the lode is better than expected and will start mining by September next year.

--With the bill passed by Parliament last week banks will be given priority over the Social Security Foundation (IKA) to be paid debts owed by denationalised enterprises facing liquidation, a factor which will further cause problems for the overburdened pension fund. IKA already has employers owing it 400 billion drachmas.

--A significant number of foreign institutional investors - the majority of whom have yet to place funds with the Athens Stock Exchange - will take part in the presentation of a select number of Greek firms due to take place in Athens on June 12-13. Organised by Societe General, OTE, National Bank, Alpha Credit Bank, Titan Cement, 3E, Attica Enterprises and METKA will present their wares to an audience including Victoire, CDC, Flemings, John Covette, Ivory and Sime, Fidelity and Delaware International.

--The government will present 10 measures to combat unemployment at imminent talks with unions and employers. The plan, developed by experts at the national economy and labour ministries, include limited wage increases in public and private sector, gradual abolition of overtime, increased part-time positions in the public sector and restrictions on pensioners' employment.

--Three changes to the taxation system widely thought to be under consideration will lift the tax burden from wage-earners and businessmen. The measures include the indexation of the taxation scale, a changfe in the indices for cars and yachts, and readjustment of the 'objective criteria' system for merchants and self-employed professionals.

--The government's bill for the independence of the Bank of Greece, in connection with its commitment that Lucas Papademos will remain at the helm, is a decisive step towards consolidating market confidence in the Greek economy and the drachma.

--Although the Bank of Greece has fended off the attack on the drachma, safeguarding parity and interest rates, the fate of profitable funds on international markets lies with the results of Sunday's French elections, which is expected to create new conditions for the course of European monetary union.
